7.3 Deep-Dive Case Analysis: Manning Canning Kitchens Inc. v. His Majesty the King (2024 TCC 159)

In Manning Canning Kitchens Inc. v. His Majesty the King, 2024 TCC 159 (Informal Procedure, Docket 2023-2126(IT)I, decided December 13, 2024 with Amended Reasons for Judgment issued January 17, 2025 by the Honourable Justice J. Scott Bodie), the Tax Court of Canada provided a detailed application of the five Northwest Hydraulic criteria to an experimental development claim83:

items: Facts of the Case: Manning Canning Kitchens Inc., a Toronto food and beverage company founded by Christine Manning, undertook a project during its taxation year ended July 31, 2020, to develop a new “better-for-you” vinegar-based soda containing cold-pressed fruit juice (commercialized as Chrisoda) that could be canned and remain shelf-stable at room temperature for at least two years without refrigeration or standard heat pasteurization83. Because unpasteurized fruit juice is “dirty by nature,” early development trials suffered microbial growth inside the cans, generating oxygen that caused the cans to explode83. At the time, no canned, shelf-stable, cold-pressed juice drink existed on the market83. On November 15, 2021, the Minister of National Revenue disallowed the 2020 SR&ED claim, arguing the project was standard product development83.
Court’s Analysis of the Five Northwest Hydraulic Criteria:

Criterion 1 (Technological Risk or Uncertainty): The Minister argued that extending shelf life could be solved via routine refrigeration or standard chemical preservatives (potassium sorbate or sodium benzoate)83. Justice Bodie rejected this argument, accepting that room-temperature shelf stability without ruining the product’s taste and appearance was the constant technical objective83. Manning Canning collaborated with Chinova Bioworks to test Chiber (an extract of white button mushrooms that had previously only been used in dairy products and never in canned cold-pressed juice beverages)83. Resolving the exploding-can problem via Chiber and specific formulation balances constituted a true technological uncertainty that routine engineering could not solve83.

Criterion 2 (Formulation of Hypotheses): Manning Canning systematically formulated hypotheses aimed at eliminating the uncertainty, including testing whether natural preservatives (Chiber) could achieve shelf stability without heat pasteurization, whether packaging in an opaque aluminum can (eliminating light exposure) would limit microbial growth, and testing specific ratio combinations of concentrate, water, carbonation, Brix (sugar/density levels), and pH (acidity levels)83.

Criterion 3 (Accordance with the Scientific Method): Working with Hale Foods (a food scientist with over 35 years of international experience), Manning Canning designed a structured, step-by-step experimental testing tree, systematically varying, measuring, and recording water/concentrate volumes, carbonation, pH, and Brix across room-temperature and refrigerated trials83.

Criterion 4 (Technological Advancement): By successfully developing a novel application for Chiber in beverages and bringing Chrisoda to market, Manning Canning demonstrated to the broader food and beverage industry that a shelf-stable, canned, cold-pressed juice drink was technologically feasible, advancing general knowledge in the field83.

Criterion 5 (Detailed Contemporaneous Record-Keeping): Sampling records submitted at trial documented specific test dates, hypotheses, measurements, and outcomes throughout the 2020 taxation year83. Justice Bodie noted that even if technical records appear complex to outsiders, their primary purpose is to allow the researcher to track hypotheses and experimental progress, which Manning Canning’s records satisfied83.

body.text: 8. Comprehensive Audit Readiness and Compliance Checklist for Canadian Claimants
To ensure full statutory compliance and audit readiness under Canada’s post-Bill C-15 SR&ED regime, claimants and tax advisors should execute the following nine-step compliance checklist:

items: Apply the $6 Million Limit and Evaluate the CCPC Gross Revenue Election (ITA 127(10.2), 127(10.31) & 127(10.6)): For taxation years beginning after December 15, 2024, apply the $6,000,000 enhanced expenditure limit (up to $2,100,000 in refundable credits) and the $15M–$75M phase-out range1. If a CCPC has raised equity that pushes its prior-year taxable capital employed in Canada above $15 million, evaluate filing the annual election under subsection 127(10.31) (or 127(10.32) for associated groups) to use the three-year average gross revenue test instead1. Confirm whether public company claimants qualify as Eligible Canadian Public Corporations (ECPCs)1.

Track and Separate Restored Capital, SUE, and Lease Expenditures After December 15, 2024: Separate capital expenditures from current expenditures, as enhanced 35% ITCs on current expenditures are 100% refundable whereas enhanced 35% ITCs on capital expenditures are 40% refundable (subsection 127.1(2.01))1. Maintain operating-time logs for new equipment, GPUs, and lab apparatus acquired after December 15, 2024, to substantiate either ≥90% ASA intended use (Lines 262 and 263 of Form T661) or >50% to <90% actual operating time for Shared-Use Equipment (SUE) (Line 504)4.

Utilize the Optional Pre-Claim Approval Process (Launched April 1, 2026): For CCPCs, Canadian corporations, and partnerships in good standing with gross business income under $25 million, consider applying for Pre-Claim Approval via My Business Account prior to starting new R&D projects to secure an 8-week eligibility determination (valid for up to 3 years) and cut post-filing expenditure review processing times from 180 days to 90 days (Lines 212 and 214 of Form T661)4.

Model the Irrevocable Proxy (55%) vs. Traditional Method Election (ITA 37(10)): Model both overhead methods before filing the initial Form T661 for the year, as the selection is irrevocable once filed12. Verify that the Prescribed Proxy Amount is computed at 55% of the Salary Base (Regulation 2900(4)) and remember that cloud computing costs can only be claimed separately under the Traditional Method (Line 360)3.

Enforce Specified Employee Caps and the 180-Day Payment Deadlines: Exclude all bonuses, profit-based remuneration, taxable benefits, and prior-year unpaid wages (Line 310) from the PPA Salary Base (Regulation 2900(9)), strip specified employee bonuses entirely (subsection 37(9)), cap each specified employee’s PPA Salary Base at the lesser of 75% of total salary or 2.5 × YMPE ($178,250 for 2025; $186,500 for 2026; $191,750 for 2027) prorated by days employed (Regulation 2900(7)), and pay all accrued wages (subsection 78(4)) and current non-salary expenses (subsection 127(26)) within 180 days of tax year-end15.

Align Form T661 Narratives with the “Why” and “How” Requirements and CRDC Codes: Enter the 5-digit Statistics Canada CRDC 2020 Version 2.0 Field of Research code (RDF#####) on Line 207 of Form T6614. Have qualified technical personnel draft concise Section B project descriptions clearly stating the baseline knowledge insufficiency (scientific or technological uncertainty), the formulated hypotheses, the systematic experimental testing or analysis, and the resulting conceptual knowledge or technological advancement20.

Maintain Contemporaneous Documentation and 6-Year Record Retention: Log hypotheses, experimental parameters, test trees, and results as the work occurs (rather than reconstructing them at year-end) and track employee time by project1. Retain all technical and financial records, vouchers, and contracts for at least 6 years from the end of the last taxation year to which they relate under paragraph 230(4)(b)3.

Coordinate Provincial Credits, Waivers, and Clean Economy ITCs: Account for provincial rules: claim the permanent $6M-aligned BC SR&ED credit (Form T666); transition to Quebec’s 30%/20% CRIC (including pre-commercialization and equipment costs) and 2% IDCI (Form CO-737.18.CI); consider waiving the 3.5% non-refundable Ontario ORDTC (Schedule 508, subsection 43(1)) in loss years so it does not reduce the 35% cash-refundable federal credit; file AT1 Schedule 29 in Alberta for the 20% IEG; and ensure no single capital asset is double-claimed under both SR&ED and the Clean Technology ITC (Section 127.45)2.

Enforce the Strict 18-Month Statutory Reporting Deadline: File Form T661 and Schedule T2SCH31 (including complete Part 9 claim preparer disclosures to avoid the $1,000 penalty) no later than 18 months after the corporate taxation year-end under subsection 37(11) and paragraph 127(9)(m), recognizing that the Income Tax Act provides no mechanism, appeal, or ministerial discretion to extend an expired SR&ED filing window3.
